title: Dark Moment
paragraphs: Maya isolated like a system shutting nonessential processes.

Not cabin 8145 first — Ethan might be there with his stillness and his *I need a minute* hardening into sentences she didn't have. She took the observation deck instead: night air, glass, wind hard enough to sting her eyes. Black ocean. Ship lights still performing romance for people whose floors hadn't just ended something in public.

Her hands found the rail and wouldn't let go. Numbers arrived without permission: Willow & Oak. March 6. Just over three weeks. Eighty-five hundred dollars of Gloria and Rafael's pride sitting in a contract. Roughly a hundred and ten save-the-dates already on other people's fridges. A dress waiting for pins. Sofia's face. Luca's onesie. Rafael's quiet handshake. Gloria's love turning sharp with grief. The reliable one — the brand she lived in — cracking into the worst version of herself in every room that loved her.
*If I leave a good man, I am the villain in every room that loves me.*

Ethan's still face on the dance-floor edge. His corridor *please.* Julian's offer on the promenade: stay in daylight, or disappear. Under wind she could not hold the difference between honesty and erasure. Her stomach cramped. Showcase dress clung damp at the spine. The ring bit her finger when she flexed. She decided — wrong, precise, adult — that the right thing was to put the wanting back in a drawer, push Julian away, and walk toward March like duty and goodness were the same word.
She found Julian near the late corridor to Compass & Low — or he found her; ship's bad talent for almosts — and pushed before he could offer softness.

"Don't stay," Maya said, clipped, managing mode as weapon against herself. "Disappear. The option you gave. I need to do the right thing — Ethan, my parents, the deposit. I'm the reliable one. Reliable people don't blow up a garden for a week on a ship. I was wrong to ask you onto that floor. Go. Please. Let me put the wanting back in a drawer and walk toward March like this was fever."
Julian went very still. Not cruel. Hurt in economical lines. "That's fear talking. You know it when you're not panicking."
"I know enough to choose him tonight." Her voice did not shake; her hands did, hidden in the folds of the dress. "Don't text. Don't find me on decks. Disappear so I can be good."

He looked at her a long time — eyes that stayed even while exiting. Then nodded once, respecting the push-away without agreeing it was wisdom. "I'll respect this. I won't chase. I'll leave you one true thing before Miami — a note, not a hunt. Daylight if you ask later, or gone. I'm sorry about his face. Good night, Maya."

He walked away. Maya stood in the corridor and felt the loneliest win of her life settle in her throat like ash: she had ordered out the man who matched her frequency to keep rooms from grieving her reliability yet. Wanting locked in a drawer that already wouldn't hold. Ethan still somewhere in 8145's weather with his stillness. March still approaching. The ship still lying about rescue.

She took the observation-deck stairs two at a time and sat on the cold bench until the showcase dress felt ridiculous. Wind. Metal under her palms. She whispered into the glass, "I'm sorry," to everyone and no one — Ethan, Julian, Gloria, herself — and the glass offered nothing back. Then she walked toward 8145 past late passengers who might have seen the dance, and did not inventory their whispers.

Inside: brittle weather beginning. His stillness transferred from theater corridor to shared carpet. Her successful push sitting in her throat like victory made of ash. She sat on the bed edge and did not touch him and did not sleep. Hull vibration counted toward approach lights. Tonight belief belonged to panic. Tonight Julian was gone by her order. Tonight Ethan was quiet beside a woman who had danced the truth and then fled into reliable performance.
She whispered to the dark that duty was not goodness and heard herself not believe it yet. Belief would be land work — fluorescent silence, fitting pins, a morning bathroom, bare hands. Not tonight.
